design:
D1 Hazard and rollback (Tier 2). The migration runs on the operator's real :8000 database at its next restart, and the bundle reaches :8000's app at its next reload, in either order. Rollback is the downgrade: enabled and runner_id go back to the two project columns, the table is dropped; only the per-job model is lost, and it did not exist before. The project columns are kept, unread, so the downgrade has somewhere to write; a later cleanup drops them.

D2 Migration number decided at build. Tonight's night window may add a migration (run-cap) on its branch from 0122; building this on master at the same time would leave two heads. This change is built after the night branch is merged and takes the next number then.

D3 Compatibility over removal. The settings body forbids unknown fields, so removing the two fields would break saving any project setting from an app window still on the old bundle; keeping them, backed by the job row, costs one mapping and keeps every existing client and test.

D4 Firings are events, not a table. EventLog already carries project-scoped, typed, timestamped JSON and is where the titler records today; a manager_job_fired type filtered by job is enough for the activity list. A table can come when a job needs to query firings by more than job and time.

D5 Only spawns are recorded. Most titling calls exit before a spawn (already titled from this excerpt, F422); recording those would make the activity list mostly noise.

D6 The registry is code, rows are configuration. A job's key, title, description and trigger ship with the Hub; the table holds only what the operator chooses. A job with no row is disabled with nothing chosen.

lifecycle: Folds into the conversation and Hub-settings capabilities when closed; the roadmap's manager-framework slice is then done.
problem: The Hub already runs model work in the background that no user starts: conversation titles (hub/hub/conversation_titles.py). Its configuration is two hard-wired project columns (models.py:98-105), which cannot name a model, so a title costs whatever the chosen runner's model costs. Nothing records what a background spawn did: the titler writes a conversation_titled event on success only, and every failure is a silent debug log. The knowledge vault roadmap adds several more jobs (distil, find contradictions, answer reports, check specs), each with a different cost and quality need; the operator asked for one page to choose the model for each (2026-10-09). Without a job table and an activity record, every new job would add two more project columns and another invisible spawn.

requirements.rationale: The page and agents read one list; a job that has never been configured is still a job the operator can turn on.
requirements.statement: GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/manager/jobs MUST answer 200 with {"jobs": [...]}, one entry per registered job in registry order, each with key, title, description, trigger, enabled, runner_id and model; a job with no stored row MUST be listed with enabled false and runner_id and model null.

requirements.rationale: Same validation as the project settings route applies to conversation_title_runner_id today (projects.py:516-528).
requirements.statement: PATCH /api/v1/projects/{id}/manager/jobs/{key} with any of enabled, runner_id and model MUST store them and answer the job as listed; an unknown key MUST answer 404, and a runner_id that is not one of this project's runners MUST answer 400 and change nothing.

requirements.rationale: Today's behaviour (conversation_titles.py:200-216, 235), with the model now choosable per job.
requirements.statement: A conversation MUST be given a generated title only while its project's conversation-titles job is enabled; the spawn MUST use the job's runner, else the conversation's agent's bound runner, and the job's model, else that runner's model. Truncation stays the floor: a disabled job, an unresolvable runner or a failed spawn leaves the truncated title.

requirements.rationale: Most title calls end before a spawn (already titled from this excerpt, F422); recording those would bury the firings that cost something.
requirements.statement: Every manager spawn MUST record one manager_job_fired event holding job, trigger, subject (for titles, the conversation id), runner_id, cli, model, outcome (written, empty or failed), detail (for titles, the title written), duration_ms and usage (null when the runner reports none). An exit before any spawn MUST record nothing.

requirements.rationale: A background agent whose work cannot be inspected is the hardest kind to trust (R5).
requirements.statement: GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/manager/activity MUST answer {"firings": [...]}, newest first, at most limit entries (default 50, at most 200), optionally filtered by job.

requirements.rationale: turn_scheduler.schedule_agent and trigger_agent_directly gate on a running Run under the agent's name (conversation_titles.py:7-13).
requirements.statement: A manager firing MUST NOT create a Run row or hold an agent name, so it never makes an agent look busy or delays that agent's queue.

requirements.rationale: The settings body forbids unknown fields (projects.py:84), so an app window still running the old bundle would otherwise fail to save any project setting until reloaded; existing clients and tests keep their contract.
requirements.statement: GET and PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}/settings MUST keep conversation_title_mode and conversation_title_runner_id: reading reports generate when the conversation-titles job is enabled and its runner_id, and writing sets the job's enabled flag and runner_id.

requirements.rationale: It runs on :8000's real database at its next restart; titles must keep behaving as configured, and rolling back must lose nothing that existed before.
requirements.statement: The migration MUST create manager_jobs and give every project whose conversation_title_mode is generate or whose conversation_title_runner_id is set a conversation-titles row (enabled exactly when the mode is generate, runner_id copied, model null); its downgrade MUST write each row's enabled flag and runner_id back to the project columns and drop the table.

requirements.rationale: A committed bundle reaches :8000's app on its next reload, possibly before its server restarts.
requirements.statement: The app's Environment MUST have a Manager section listing each job with an on/off control, a runner select and a model select, and below them the activity list; the Settings section MUST no longer show the conversation title controls. Where the Hub answers 404 for the manager routes, the section MUST say this Hub has no manager yet instead of failing.

in_scope: A registry of manager jobs in Hub code, holding one job in this slice: conversation-titles
A manager_jobs table: per project and job, enabled, runner id and model
Routes to list jobs, change one, and list recent firings
Conversation titling reads its job row: enabled, runner (else the conversation's agent's runner, as today), model (else the runner's model)
A firing record for every manager spawn, as an event
The project settings route keeps conversation_title_mode and conversation_title_runner_id, backed by the job row
A migration copying today's settings into the job table, with a lossless downgrade
An Environment > Manager section in the app: jobs with on/off, runner and model, and the activity list; the title controls leave the Settings section
non_goals: Moving checkpoint generation (checkpoint_runner_id, checkpoint_model) into the manager: it has its own thresholds and cutover policy and moves in its own change
Any vault job: they arrive with their slices
Dropping the two project columns: they stay in place, unread, and are dropped by a later cleanup migration so this downgrade loses nothing
Cost in money: a firing records the usage the runner reports, and nothing when it reports none

summary: A project gets a Manager section listing the Hub's background jobs. Each job can be turned on or off and given its own runner and model, and an activity list shows every time a job spawned a model: which job, for what, with which runner and model, how it ended, how long it took and what it used. Conversation titling is the first job: its two project settings move into a per-job table by migration, and the project settings route keeps accepting and returning them so nothing that already works stops working. Tier 2: a migration, plus a UI bundle that reaches :8000's app on its next reload.
